correctness.rationale: The final degree-weighted cooperator mass is a bounded martingale whose absorption limit is exactly the fixation indicator on any finite connected graph. Uniform initial cooperator yields constant first-stage expectation. A direct 3x3 eigen-decomposition yields the exact finite-g probability. The increment numerator and 5-node degrees certify the strict maximum at g=2; an exact 4-node edge-attachment classification proves minimality; integer inequalities prove unbounded tree optimizers. Standalone exact rational script verifies 1,416 assertions including an independently solved 32-state absorbing Markov chain. Only the analytically proved scope is accepted.

originality.rationale: The source paper investigates precisely finite-stage growing-network death-birth dynamics and reports increasing g-fixation on studied topologies, with a sufficient monotonicity statement under regularity. Our claim instead exhibits and minimizes a nonmonotonic finite-g phenomenon among all admissible connected growth schedules and gives arbitrary late unique optima on a tree family. It does not claim the degree martingale or matrix evolution as new. Direct comparison was made with the relevant main article, earlier full preprint, switching-network paper, search literature and semantic database records.
